flagged_rules.impact: गम् etc. take Ātmanepada after सम् when used intransitively (अकर्मक, 1.3.26): गङ्गा यमुनया संगच्छते. With an object they stay Parasmaipada: ग्रामं संगच्छति.

जि takes Ātmanepada after वि and परा: विजयते, पराजयते. Both are active and mean “conquers / overcomes”. With an ablative of what one cannot bear, परा + जि means “is worn out by” (1.4.26 पराजेरसोढः). “Is defeated” is the passive पराजीयते.

flagged_rules.phenomenon: Sūtras 6.1.137 सम्परिभ्यां करोतौ भूषणे, 6.1.138 समवाये च, 6.1.139 उपात्प्रतियत्नवैकृतवाक्याध्याहारेषु
flagged_rules.impact: कृ takes सुट् (स्) after सम् and परि when adorning is meant, after सम् also when assembling is meant, and after उप in the listed senses: संस्करोति, परिष्करोति, उपस्कृतम्. Otherwise: संकरोति.
स् of सद् becomes ष् after an upasarga ending in इ or उ, except प्रति: निषीदति, विषीदति, परिषीदति; but प्रतिसीदति. The old file called this sūtra “सदिपरस्य”, which does not exist.
न् of a root taught with ण् becomes ण् after र्/ष् in an upasarga: प्रणमति, प्रणयति, परिणयति. Roots like नृत्, नन्द्, नर्द् are not णोपदेश, so प्रनृत्यति keeps न्.
After उद्, स् of स्था/स्तम्भ् is replaced by a sound like the preceding one: उत्तिष्ठति. The old file quoted the sūtra as “उदो निष्ठातस्तयोः पूर्वस्य”.

flagged_rules.phenomenon: दुस्, दुर्, सु with finite verbs
flagged_rules.impact: These are used mainly before kṛt forms, especially खल् (3.3.126): दुस्तरः, दुर्लभः, दुर्बोधः, सुकरः. Finite verbs दुस्तरति, दुर्लभते, दुर्बुध्यते are not attested; दुश्चरति, सुचरति, सुतिष्ठति are rare. सु in the sense of praise is a karmapravacanīya (1.4.94) and causes no ष्.
UDC-000101 to UDC-000140 had the same meaningless example (“… साधुः स्वधर्मेण”) and auto-generated notes. Examples were replaced by constructed sentences (marked as such); notes were cleared.

previous_flagged_rules.impact: Root gam (परस्मैपदी) becomes आत्मनेपदी when prefixed with sam (संगच्छते, not संगच्छति in the sense of harmony/union).
Root ji (परस्मैपदी) becomes आत्मनेपदी when prefixed with vi or parā (विजयते, पराजयते).
Root kṛ takes suṭ-āgama (स्) after sam and pari when adornment/refinement is meant (संस्करोति, परिष्करोति).
Root sad undergoes retroflexion (ṣatva) after ni, vi, pari (निषीदति, विषीदति, परिषीदति).
Roots with initial n take ṇ after r/ṣ in upasargas like pra, pari, nir (प्रणमति, प्रणयति, परिणयति).
